title: Begin, My Tongue, Some Heavenly Theme
description: Begin, My Tongue, Some Heavenly Theme in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 69, headed “The faithfulness of God in his promises”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-gin, my tongue, some heav-enly theme, And speak some bound-less thing, The might-y works, or might-ier name Of our e-ter-nal King.

lines: Begin, my tongue, some heavenly theme,
The mighty works, or mightier name
Sing the sweet promise of his grace,
His hand has writ the sacred word
Nor can the powers of darkness rase
He that can dash whole worlds to death
And make them when he please,
He speaks, and that almighty breath
His very word of grace is strong
As that which built the skies,
The voice that rolls the stars along
He said, "Let the wide heaven be spread,"
"Abrah'm, I'll be thy God," he said,
O, might I hear thine heavenly tongue
Those gentle words should raise my song
How would my leaping heart rejoice

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
